To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Q148R minority variant were frequently detected, at low-level, both in integrase-experienced and integrase-naive patients.
Q148R variants are frequent, but not always associated with virologic failure.
Q148R minority mutants are frequently detected in integrase-naïve HIV-infected patients, and their impact on long term viral suppression needs to further investigated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the prevalence of minority integrase variants in HIV-infed patients.
the study of the HIV-1 integrase protein and its interaction with the cellular cofactors, which are required for its function.
the detection of minority variants harbored by integrase inhibitors-naive HIV-inflicted patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of Q/R148H minority variants in integrase-naïve patients should not be a reason for concern.
the presence of integrase Q-148R minority variants does not predict virological failure in patients initiating raltegravir-containing regimens.

Q148R minority mutants are not a cause for concern in terms of virological response to integrase inhibitors, but they may have a potential to become dominant in patients with delayed response to therapy or in patients with virological failures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of Q151R minority variants is frequent in integrase-naïve HIV-infected patients and is not associated with an increased risk of failure under raltegravir.

the prevalence of Q148R and K103N minority mutations is high in both antiretrovial-experienced and -naive patients, but their impact on virological failure is not consistent and needs to be further studied.
Q148R minority variant is a common polymorphism in HIV infected patients, but it may have an impact on viral replication.
The main takeaway from our work is that

integrase resistance testing should be considered in patients failing integrase inhibitor-based regimens, especially in patients with low-level resistance to nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors.
the presence of Q/R/H minority variants in integrase-naïve patients is not a contraindication for initiating an integrase inhibitor-based regimen.
integrase inhibitors should be used with caution in patients harboring minority variants harboring Q148H, R or N155H.
